title: Make the go-or-wait decision on a retained throw
stage_label: Separate instructional session · Week 2, Day 4 · individually authored · written athletic design reviewed
status_note: Independent source, written programming and numeric reviews passed. The companion audit covers 7,776 timing scenarios, 216 mixed triad patterns and 52 rejecting probes. Current canonical release, actual facilities/athlete histories and precise separate tumbling remain unverified.
brief: Today teaches one early THROW/HOLD decision on a genuinely retained stationary chest projection. Full preparation rehearses the owned arm path and handling. The first existing main opportunity is a counted known-cue E0 rehearsal with complete retrieval; E1 uses only the remaining actual opportunity prefix for choice learning. Push/pull go first in Strength, followed by familiar knee, hip and brace work. Keep actual ball, direction, intent, strength setup and recent smaller doses. Attention and equipment conduct are the instructional targets; no reaction-time improvement or harder throwing is promised.
quality_target: On an individually addressed early cue, the athlete either uses the owned release or keeps the ball, parks it and waits. Record the actual cue, response, movement quality and retrieval conduct separately. A first choice can be useful learning without proving repeatability or both rules. No percentage quota, distance target score or speed contest is used.
continuity: Actual OR-05/direct stable throw and known-release/retrieval, plus the most recent OR-08/direct support-dose and response record → known E0 rehearsal and only remaining OR-09 choices → OR-13 applies its separately qualified cue/movement branch → OR-17 observes that actual retained branch with reduced prompting. Dates and missing attendance do not manufacture history.
audience: Separate instructional on-ramp; 15 athletes, three lanes and two qualified coaches are planning assumptions. Ages 12–14 are the reference, not a novice label. All three age groups receive explicit doses and the same task-specific entry decisions; older athletes do not automatically receive a larger ball or more choices. Directly competent athletes may use their separately qualified main branch instead of unnecessary remedial attendance.
readiness: Before the new choice, require repeatable actual same-demand stationary throwing, comfortable arm path, secure ball/chest handling, actual floor pickup/carry/set-down, understood and repeatable known-cue/retrieval behavior, fitting rack access and current suitable response. Confirm both signal meanings verbally, with no extra athlete practice release. The current E0 rehearsal must remain suitable before E1. Prior whole go/no-go mastery is not needed for its first counted instruction. An emerging throw or new implement uses known-cue instruction instead. Each no-release alternative and strength role retains independent gates. Pain, distress, restrictions, uncontained ball, unsafe traffic or loss of control ends the affected task; no additional test secures clearance.
equipment_space: PLANNING ONLY: 15 athletes, 2 qualified coaches, 3 parallel throw lanes, each 3 m wide × 6 m protected forward length, with additional 1 m side buffer between lanes, a rear queue/set-up area and unobstructed coach access. No athlete waits in a target lane. A broad optional first-landing reference band 1–3 m ahead helps explain forward direction; it is not a distance requirement, floor slam target or score. The ball follows a natural forward arc and lands by gravity. Lane perimeter/soft containment must stop the actual ball without hazardous rebound, crossing into a neighbor, or contact with a person; six metres is a planning test, not a guaranteed containment distance. Before use the coaches inspect actual ball behavior and the complete retrieval route. If containment is not verified, use a no-release task, not an improvised wall or partner throw. Three intact soft low-rebound medicine balls, one per active lane, and three stable racks at comfortable hand height for E1 are required; P2 uses three marked floor-ball spots with a clear 1 m out-and-back carrying space behind the throw line; size/type/mass may differ by actual athlete fit. Reference 0.5 kg / 18 cm is a proposed equipment test point, not a uniform mandatory load. Actual values must be recorded and replacements inspected; no automatic heavier age tier. The standardized preparation retains 15 personal 3 × 3 m bays. Strength requires five suitable high pressing surfaces (90 cm reference only), five suitable benches and five manageable dumbbells for rows, five mats; supports can be reused sequentially if each purpose fits and the transition is verified. Breathing alternative needs five lower-leg supports; suspension alternative needs five independently verified secure anchors. Quantity, dimensions, sightlines and equipment fit remain unverified. For this reference clock, each lane’s declared ball and fixed rack must fit every assigned athlete who uses it; ball/rack changes are not hidden inside a zero-time handover. If actual changes or slower instruction are required, delay/omit later work within the component or select an independently eligible no-release task. The retained familiar DB hip option additionally needs five fitting elevated stations and ten simultaneously suitable DBs; two coaches observe two/three independently familiar athletes. Between-wave handling reset has its own 20 s allowance. Actual inventory, each assigned athlete’s fit and combined bay/lane sightlines must be verified.
coaching_flow: Keep athlete order 0–14. P1 has three groups of five in personal bays; P2 has five triads. Main actions are sequential within each triad: one addressed athlete at a time on15 s slots. Others keep balls parked and wait behind their own line. Both coaches can observe the active cue; one then watches released-ball owners while the other watches rear queues/racks. HOLD/no-release athletes do not retrieve. All lanes close before collection, and an immediate fault cancels later actions until safe. Stationary alternatives stay in visible personal bays; no imaginary return or unseen transfer. Strength has three waves of five in each sequential role, observed two/three per coach. Actual one-to-one teaching needs reduce or defer later work.

time_rules: All demonstrations, readiness discussion, ball/rack setup, actions, shutdown, retrieval, water and transitions stay inside the stated windows. Release times are earliest starts; actual slower handling or a fault delays/omits later work. Do not force pace, shorten required recovery, remove the full base or add opportunities to fill an empty slot.
preparation_note: Use the unchanged instructional standard/compact base fully resolved below. The two targets use40 s P1 unloaded position and140 s P2 no-release floor handling. The explicit OR-09 amendment places one complete familiar throw rehearsal in counted E0 within the existing main opportunity ceiling. Neither preparation task throws or supplies a cue/throw pass.

exercises.name: Rehearse the owned unloaded chest-start arm path
exercises.set_purpose: One unloaded reach-and-return rehearses the retained arm path and organized standing without spending a throwing opportunity. Quiet standing replaces it only under its own comfort gate.
exercises.execution: Remain in the personal bay. Feet comfortably apart and planted, knees unlocked. Set hands comfortably at chest level for 2 s, reach both arms forward for 2 s, return for 2 s, relax/reset for 4 s. No ball, preload, forced shoulder position or lower-body movement. Use relaxed open hands with palms facing forward and fingers comfortably upward, as if supporting the back/sides of a small ball. Keep wrists comfortable and elbows below shoulder height without pinning them to the ribs. Reach only through a comfortable owned range; record any adapted orientation.
exercises.cues: Feet still; comfortable chest start; reach forward; return and relax.
exercises.errors: Arching, shrugging, forcing elbow lock, dipping to create momentum, adding repetitions while watching another group, or treating this as a push-up/row pass.
exercises.rationale: Keep the same low-demand OR-05 position rehearsal before handling. No new cue choice, throw or upper-body fatigue is added.
exercises.metadata: Method: one observed position rehearsal. Tenets: Strength / Body Control; integrated coordination. Pattern: bilateral reach. Equipment: personal bay. Local teaching record, not a released profile.

exercises.competency: All ages require comfortable standing and the assigned unloaded reach. A first visitor may learn this single counted action after demonstration. If upper-body reach is unavailable but standing is comfortable, use the explicit 10 s quiet-standing route. That route gives no arm-path evidence. Experienced athletes keep the small dose and actual comfortable range.
exercises.progression: Retain one listed action with the actual suitable ball/range where applicable. No added throw, fit trial or second handling attempt. A partial or failed action is counted and may require deferral; changing age is not a progression.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR-05/direct arm-path control → one retained OR-09 position rehearsal → counted E0 known task, then only independently eligible E1 cue instruction.

exercises.name: Rehearse floor handling and chest position without a release
exercises.mapping: BALL-HOLD-TEACH; unloaded/standing options are separate tasks
exercises.set_purpose: One counted floor pickup, 5 s chest hold, 2 m out-and-back carry, floor set-down and exit rehearses equipment control. It has zero throws and observes no cue inhibition.
exercises.execution: Begin with the ball resting on a marked floor spot behind the throw line. After demonstration, use a comfortable bilateral hip/knee bend to pick it up to chest level over 5 s, hold comfortably for 5 s, walk 1 m out and 1 m back in the marked personal handling area over 4 s (2 s walking plus 2 s turning), set the ball back on its original floor spot over 6 s, then exit/reset over 4 s. The ball stays in two hands until set-down. This counted handling loop includes floor access and 2 m loaded carry; no throw, catch, loaded push-out, extra trial, or passing to a child. Do not force a floor reach that is unavailable or hurry the turn; stop the action and let the coach manage the implement if needed. Use both palms/finger pads on the rear-side surfaces of the ball, thumbs comfortably behind it and fingers spread enough for a secure grip; no forced thumb shape or joint angle. Keep wrists comfortable and elbows below shoulder height. Ball rests in the hands at chest level, not squeezed against the throat. Declare the individually fitting contact and retain it across P2/E1; a ball requiring painful wrist position or an insecure spread is unsuitable.
exercises.cues: Reach the floor comfortably before taking the ball; two hands; stand still for the hold; walk and turn on instruction; return and set down gently.
exercises.errors: Releasing on a setup cue, dropping the ball, prolonged unsupported waiting, forcing grip on a large implement, holding breath, or awarding a throwing/cue-speed pass.
exercises.rationale: A complete familiar release and whole-group retrieval cannot be assumed to fit the 140 s preparation target. The explicit amendment retains handling here and assigns one counted known-cue rehearsal to E0 within the existing total main opportunity limit.
exercises.metadata: Method: observed floor handling and waiting instruction. Tenets: Body Control / Strength; equipment conduct and attention integrated. Pattern: one floor pickup, chest hold, short walking carry/turn and floor set-down. Equipment: declared soft medicine ball, marked original floor spot and a separate unobstructed 1 m out-and-back path per lane; no shared crossing.

exercises.competency: First-visit handling is taught within this counted set after the coach has selected a plausible comfortable implement by size and prior information. This set provides the actual fit/handling observation; no prior successful ball hold is invented. If grip or position is unsuitable, set down with coach management and end the action; select a separately eligible unloaded or standing route for later work. Record partial handling, not a pass. No more ball trials are added. Comfortable ordinary walking/turning is required for the carry. Comfortable unloaded floor access is independently established or observed during the initial reach of this same counted P2 pickup before accepting the ball load. An owned partial-range hinge/squat does not establish floor access. If that initial reach is unavailable or uncomfortable, do not lift: end the assigned action, have the coach manage the ball and use a separately eligible no-ball task later. This is one counted pickup opportunity, not an extra screening repetition; the 5 s envelope may be delayed for instruction. A smaller independent P2 route does not grant or revoke main throwing evidence; actual floor handling, rack fit, release and conduct must each suit the selected main task today.
exercises.progression: Retain one listed action with the actual suitable ball/range where applicable. No added throw, fit trial or second handling attempt. A partial or failed action is counted and may require deferral; changing age is not a progression.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR-05/direct floor handling and current comfort → one counted handling rehearsal or eligible unloaded/standing replacement → known E0 with its own gates. Neither P2 handling nor a first E0 release alone qualifies the new cue choice.

exercises.name: Rehearse the known task within the first counted main opportunity
exercises.mapping: CHEST-PASS-TEACH — proposed local known-release / go-no-go contexts; canonical profile-versus-card identity and current release remain unresolved. See prescriptions/OR09_LIBRARY_MAPPING.md.
exercises.set_purpose: Use the first existing main opportunity to rehearse the exact known throw on an early individual THROW cue and observe current retrieval conduct. This is one of the total 3/2/2/1 opportunities, not an extra preparation release. Known-cue instruction or a separate no-release task remains available when throwing is emerging or unavailable.
exercises.execution: Use the actual fitting ball in both hands at chest height, palms/finger pads on its rear-side surfaces, thumbs comfortably behind and wrists comfortable. Keep elbows below shoulder height and both feet planted in the owned bilateral stance. Only the addressed athlete picks up from the fitting rack. On the early individual THROW cue, project forward with the same smooth quick easy intent, no dip, step, jump or rotation; finish balanced without a catch or chase. Wait behind the line. Before collection every action must have stopped, every actually released ball settled and every retained ball securely parked. Only released-ball owners retrieve after global all-clear, using their own unobstructed lane and ordinary controlled pickup/carry to the rack. A mixed triad need not release three balls. No-release alternatives follow their own complete action and remain behind the line or in the assigned visible bay.
exercises.cues: Your lane; wait for your name and throw cue; send it forward; stay at the line; retrieve only together; carry it back.
exercises.errors: Throwing on another athlete’s cue, chasing a ball before all-clear, rapid partner exchange, adding a step/dip, throwing toward people, arching, choosing a heavier ball to reach a target, or treating a known permission cue as a measured reaction test.
exercises.rationale: Resolve the outline’s familiar release rehearsal inside the main allocation with a complete release/shutdown/retrieval clock. Prior stable task evidence plus this current response protects subsequent choice learning; the first-ever E0 throw cannot create prior repeatability.
exercises.metadata: Method: repeated single observed teaching attempts with complete reset. Tenets: Strength / Body Control; coordination, perception and equipment conduct integrated. Pattern: bilateral horizontal projection. Physiology: low-volume release practice; no output gain claimed. Equipment: inspected ball, rack and contained open lane.

exercises.competency: Choice-route E0 retains actual repeatable same-demand throw, handling and known-cue/retrieval behavior. For a FIRST known-cue instructional throw, require actual comfortable grip/chest setup, floor pickup/set-down and ordinary carry, comfortable unloaded arm path, understood individual permission and group retrieval rules, fitting rack access, current suitable response and physically verified containment/supervision. Prior successful throwing or a floor push-up is not required. Unknown handling stays on its separately gated no-release instruction until established. A first known-cue throw stays on the known route today; one E0 result does not supply prior repeatability for choice. E0 does not teach a choice. Stop for changed response, insecure ball, unsuitable lane/traffic or misunderstanding.
exercises.progression: Keep the actual implement, feet, no-preload start, direction, easy intent and full recovery. Cap1 and compressed L use E0 only. A fault consumes E0; it is not replaced or ignored to access E1.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR-05/direct known task → first counted E0 rehearsal today → only remaining eligible E1 opportunities; no additional rehearsal precedes them.

exercises.name: Choose THROW or HOLD while retaining the owned movement
exercises.mapping: CHEST-PASS-TEACH — proposed local known-release / go-no-go contexts; canonical profile-versus-card identity and current release remain unresolved. See prescriptions/OR09_LIBRARY_MAPPING.md.
exercises.set_purpose: Each remaining opportunity teaches one early cue interpretation while preserving the actual throw and movement demand. THROW produces one owned release; HOLD retains the ball for 3 s, parks it and waits. Both are counted. Known-cue, hold, unloaded and standing routes have their separate maintenance/instruction jobs and do not earn unobserved choice results.
exercises.execution: Use the unchanged stationary bilateral chest start and no deliberate dip, step, jump, rotation or wall/partner target. Only the addressed athlete picks up. After readiness is confirmed, the coach says exactly THROW or HOLD once. THROW retains the owned forward release and balanced finish. HOLD keeps the same two-hand chest position and both feet planted for 3 s, then lowers to the own fitting rack over a 5 s allowance and settles behind the line. No forward push-out or fake throw. Do not preannounce the next choice, accelerate cue timing or score reaction speed. Released-ball owners alone retrieve after whole-group all-clear; everyone else stays behind the line or in the assigned visible bay.
exercises.cues: Wait for your own name. Hear the whole cue. THROW: use your known throw. HOLD: keep it, park it, wait. All-clear before collection.
exercises.errors: Releasing for another athlete’s cue; turning HOLD into a throw or feint; catching/chasing; a new dip or harder throw; rushing set-down; replacing a false release; counting a canceled cue as observed; restoring extra GO attempts to match old throw totals.
exercises.rationale: Early go/no-go interpretation changes one decision demand on a genuinely retained task. First known-release learning remains a separate route. A partner/variable target pass, squat-to-wall throw or directional cut would change the movement/space contract and is not selected.
exercises.metadata: Method: low-density early go/no-go instruction with recovered individual permission. Tenets: Coordination, Body Control and Explosiveness on actual throws; Strength support remains separate. Perception/inhibition and equipment conduct are observed; no reaction-speed, sport-transfer or maximal-output result is claimed.

exercises.competency: For FIRST choice instruction, require actual repeatable same-implement/stance/direction/intent throwing, secure handling and whole known-release/retrieval behavior; confirm both word meanings before holding a ball. Prior successful go/no-go mastery is not required. Today’s E0 must also retain suitable response/conduct. A single first or emerging E0 throw cannot replace prior repeatability. For RETAINED choice work, use direct actual repeatable same-demand throw and cue behavior without requiring attendance at OR-05. If throw/cue prerequisites are missing, use the independently eligible known/no-release route or defer. One remaining choice observes only its presented rule; neither attendance nor successful HOLD alone proves both rules. Operational source approval is separately unverified.
exercises.progression: Retain the total actual main opportunity ceiling, ball, stance, direction, intent and recovery. Default E0+E1 totals standard D3/L2, compressed D2/L1. E1 after E0 is respectively2/1/1/0, before smaller cap1/2. Select HOLD→THROW or THROW→HOLD and take only the remaining prefix; never add a cue to complete both rules. Reduce or end remaining opportunities if attention or movement deteriorates. Do not count NO-GO as a missing throw owed later.
exercises.continuity: Actual OR-05/direct stable throw and known-release/retrieval, plus current E0 → first or retained early choice in remaining OR-09 opportunities → OR-13 uses only its independently qualified movement/cue branch → OR-17 observes the actual retained rule with reduced prompting, not faster cues.

timing_narrative:
**Preparation, 180 s after the full base.** P1 uses10 s reminder then groups of five at10/20/30 s, one10 s action each. P2 uses20 s gather/demo then triads at20/44/68/92/116 s, one24 s floor-handling action each:5 s pickup,5 s chest hold,4 s carry/turn,6 s floor set-down,4 s exit. Shorter unloaded/standing choices use10 s and rest for the remainder. The last triad ends at140 s. P1 rest is at least20 s; the fixed-order P1→P2 gap is at least40 s. Actual extra fit changes are not assumed to fit; omit/delay remaining work. Standing choices remain in directly visible personal bays. Main-opening setup contains any required return from P2 to those bays.

**Main setup and the first counted rehearsal.** Main-relative0–240 s covers the actual recorded route, ball/rack/containment check, cue explanation, coach demonstration, water and grouping. No extra athlete throw or test pickup occurs. E0 is the first counted main opportunity at relative240 s, using one known THROW cue or the separately eligible no-release task. First-ever or emerging throwing stays on the known route; it cannot supply prior repeatability for E1 choice. If E0 current response is unsuitable, end or simplify remaining work under its independent gates without repayment.

**One90 s triad.** Athlete starts0/15/30 s are sequential. THROW takes10 s:2 s rack pickup/chest setup,2 s readiness/individual cue,1 s release,3 s follow-through,2 s wait; the remaining5 s slot is quiet waiting. HOLD takes15 s:2 s pickup,2 s readiness/cue,3 s chest hold,5 s own-rack set-down,3 s settle behind the line. No-release hold/reach/standing uses its explicit10 s action and quiet remaining slot. Everyone stays behind the line until the scheduled phase. At45–50 s, confirm every action stopped, all held balls parked and released balls settled; every lane remains shut. Only released-ball owners retrieve at50–65 s:up to6 m outward/6 s,3 s controlled floor pickup,up to6 m loaded return/6 s. At65–75 s, owners have5 s rack set-down and5 s rear clearance; HOLD athletes perform only empty-hand rear clearance, with no second pickup/set-down or retrieval. Stationary-bay athletes stay in their bays. At75–90 s, after outgoing owners clear, the next triad walks from the rear holding marks to its own behind-line working marks/racks along an inspected unobstructed rear path. No ball is picked up during staging and no path crosses a target lane. HOLD waiting marks must leave that feed clear. The first triad stages inside opening setup; after a round the next round’s first triad stages during the final15 s before its scheduled start. The actual path and ordinary pace must fit; otherwise delay/omit. Unsafe release, intrusion or uncontrolled ball immediately closes all lanes before any scheduled later check.

**Rounds and opportunity ceilings.** Five triads start at0/90/180/270/360 s within each450 s round. E0 starts main-relative240 s. E1 rounds start780/1320 s for standard D; standard L and compressed D have only the780 s E1 round; compressed L has no E1. This retains total3/2/2/1 opportunities including E0. Cap1 keeps E0 alone; cap2 keeps E0 plus only the first E1. E1 choice uses the selected HOLD→THROW or THROW→HOLD prefix. Never append the missing cue type. The540 s interval between corresponding round starts gives at least450 s recovery after the whole90 s triad, beyond the60 s minimum. The last standard D round clears at main-relative1770 s, session44:30, leaving30 s before Strength. Compressed D clears at relative1230 s, session30:30, leaving270 s. Empty/canceled slots remain rest. The90 s gap between round clearance and the next round contains rest and next-first-triad staging in its last15 s; no extra throw occurs. No cue type or athlete choice can extend the90 s modeled triad; actual overrun triggers delay/omission.

**Strength, five familiar roles.** Standard:push45–51,pull51–57,knee57–63,hip63–69,brace69–75. Each6 min role reserves90 s setup, with five-athlete waves at90/165/240 s. Compressed:push35–39,pull39–43,knee43–47,hip47–51,brace51–55. Each4 min role reserves60 s setup, with waves at60/120/180 s. Keep the same athlete groups and observe two/three athletes per coach. Longest reference bouts are push17 s,row52 s,knee25 s,BW hip21 s,familiar DB hip26 s,heel taps26 s; breathing is40 s plus15 s quiet recovery. DB hip has10 s handling plus at most16 s repetitions and20 s between-wave reset, fitting60 s compact pitch. The last compact DB bout ends at206 s, leaving34 s in its role; its90 s recovery fits before that athlete’s brace wave. Other demanding roles retain60 s recovery; breathing retains its separately specified15 s. No additional strength set, circuit, athlete equipment race or physical finisher is added.
alternatives:
Select the main route before delivery from actual evidence. **Choice** keeps a repeatable throw and known-release/retrieval, confirms signals, uses known E0 then only remaining choices. **Known** teaches or retains the original single-cue throw under OR-05’s component gates, without prior whole-throw mastery; no choice is added today from one emerging E0 result. **Hold** uses actual comfortable ball handling and a fitting rack but never releases. **Reach** uses an independently comfortable empty-hand arm path. **Standing** requires independently comfortable quiet bilateral standing. If even that is unsuitable, defer. Any current source/variant approval still needs verification; these proposed local contexts are not approved substitutes. Search/resolve a current approved exact alternative before operational release rather than silently switching to a wall, partner, squat, catch or reactive target.

Main THROW mechanics retain both palms/finger pads on the rear-side ball surfaces, thumbs comfortably behind, comfortable wrists, elbows below shoulder height, no forced hand angle, chest-height start and balanced planted feet. workload_narrative:
Count P1 unloaded reach/standing, P2 pickup/5 s hold/2 m carry/floor set-down, E0 known-cue opportunity and each E1 cue opportunity separately. Record intended THROW/HOLD distribution, actual presented cues, correct/incorrect/ambiguous responses, actual releases including faults, post-cue holds, pickups/set-downs and owner retrieval. Never use valid responses as the physical dose counter. Three/two/two/one total main opportunities include E0; HOLD can reduce intended throws without creating a debt. A single remaining choice cannot prove both rules. Standard D choice with HOLD-first has one E0 throw, one HOLD and one THROW before any faults; smaller and reverse-order prefixes are explicit.

Ordinary floor handling and ball retrieval are not running, intentional athlete jumping or landing. All prescribed main variants keep zero intentional athlete flight events; unknown actual ordinary contacts remain unknown. Retrieval planning caps are at most6 m outward plus6 m loaded return per actual released ball, with actual distance recorded rather than presumed equal to the cap. NO-GO/no-release variants have no ball-retrieval distance; stationary bays have no lane return. Fault recovery may add actual handling that must be recorded and reduces/defer remaining work instead of being ignored. Strength remains one set each of push, pull, knee, hip and brace with its selected cap and support option. Do not sum alternative routes or timing envelopes as one athlete workout. Actual load, symptoms, cue status and completed work remain null until recorded.
final_tumbling: Standard75–90 or compressed55–60 is water/recovery, descriptive reflection, recording and transfer, with zero additional physical sets. Ask the athlete to explain the actual cue, whether the ball should have stayed or gone, and the all-clear rule; no extra athlete demonstration, penalty or throw game. Share actual shoulder/wrist/grip/trunk response, lower-body work, attention, faults and handling with the separate coach. Body Control/Tumbling remains its own30 min segment after the athletic block. Its precise approved session and exercise doses are unresolved; this handoff is not a completed tumbling prescription or advanced-skill clearance.
coach_record:
Record actual prior same-demand throw/known-cue/retrieval evidence and whether today is first choice instruction, retained choice or known/no-release learning. Enter actual ball type/kg/diameter/rebound, rack/support heights, containment and sightlines, E0 response, selected E1 cue order and opportunity cap. For each scheduled action record whether a cue was presented, which cue, actual response and releases/holds/handling; distinguish misunderstanding, distraction, fatigue and movement loss without diagnosing. Canceled cues remain unobserved. Record actual most recent knee/hip/push/pull/brace variation, load/count, newer unloading and selected reductions; unknown history is not zero or presumed completion.

Next OR-13 requires its own qualified movement branch: stationary throwing evidence does not grant a directional step, braking or reactive cut. If stable throwing and early release are separately passed while HOLD remains emerging, the main REACT-T permission may retain only that passed early-release rule under the entry matrix. OR-17 observes the actual retained cue rule with reduced prompting, not a new faster cue or harder implement. JUMP-T uses its separately qualified throwing branch without landing credit. No athlete automatically advances because OR-09 was offered or attended.
review_status: Independent source/schema and complete written programming PASS; numeric PASS for 7,776 clock cohorts, 144 reduction packets, 248,832 factored choices, 216 mixed triad patterns and 52 rejecting probes. Staged first-handling/known-release/E0/choice gates and exact pooled-ledger equality are verified. See or_09_review.md and or_09_check_results.json for scope and current fingerprints. No operational release, actual athlete result or precise separate tumbling is claimed.
outline_reconciliation: Active OR-09 amendment moves the complete familiar release rehearsal to counted E0 within the existing total main opportunity ceiling. route_policy.main_permission: REACT-T only under the separately passed actual early-release or go/no-go rule and stable throw/retrieval. Missing inhibition may retain passed known-release permission; no reactive-cut clearance. JUMP-T uses its own passed throw branch without landing credit.

signals.THROW: One owned forward chest projection to the unchanged contained lane.
signals.HOLD: Retain the ball at chest, keep both feet planted, then park on the own fitting rack without a release.

cue_response_contract.cue_delivery: Address the individual athlete, authorize only that athlete to pick up, confirm readiness, then say exactly THROW or HOLD once. The athlete knows both meanings but not the next choice. No rapid cue, startle, color-only rule or response-speed score.

HOLD.after_action: Ball remains parked. Athlete waits behind own line until the scheduled rear reset; no walk into a target lane and no second set-down.

cue_response_contract.false_release_rule: Immediately shut all lanes; cancel subsequent actions until safe. Count the cue if actually presented and every release including a premature one. Coach manages any uncontained ball; only released-ball owners retrieve after explicit all-clear when safe. No replacement cue or throw is owed.
cue_response_contract.withheld_on_THROW_rule: Record the actual cue and no release. Keep the ball secure, park under coach direction in the remaining action allowance or delay shutdown. This consumes the opportunity; do not issue another THROW.
cue_response_contract.all_clear: Before collection, every action has stopped, every released ball is settled and all held balls are securely parked. Coach confirms the entire retrieval area and queues are clear. No throw while anyone retrieves.

stationary_policy.rule: P1/P2/E0/E1 unloaded or quiet-standing choices stay in own inspected personal bays under the assigned coach’s direct view. They have no lane return or zero-time central transfer. Any transfer back after handling P2 occurs within opening main setup. Combine a bay and lane group only if actual sightlines permit both; otherwise omit/defer that combination.

age_scaling_policy.equal_dose_reason: Short low-effort preparation is not age-based overload. Explicit equal doses across ages are deliberate; task skill, body size, comfortable range and current readiness decide the variant.
age_scaling_policy.readiness_independent_of_age: Experienced younger athletes may use qualified familiar actions; unfamiliar older athletes use instruction. Age never grants flight, rapid descent, floor support, loaded patterns or cue response.

layout_and_timing_assumptions.layout: Three columns of five distinct 3 m × 3 m personal bays: 15 independent working spaces. Five athletes share a lane assignment, never an overlapping crawl corridor.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.additional_space: Unobstructed peripheral coach circulation/access/egress and separately verified start, runoff and return corridors are additional to the 9 m × 15 m bay rectangle. The marked rectangle is not the total facility footprint.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.travel: Standing paths remain in personal bays. Short forward passes are at most 1.6 m; backward/lateral spans 1 m or less except 1.5 m carioca. Individually check full hand-walk/plank footprint before use.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.orientation: All bays face one end. Complete a pass and stop before ordinary walking return within that same bay. No crossing between athletes or concurrent opposite-direction traffic inside a bay.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.coaches: Familiar shared practice: one coach scans A/B and one scans B/C with clear oblique views. Three-wave teaching/checks: both coaches watch one active lane and split five athletes 2/3; other lanes stand. Clear views of all active feet/trunks are required.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.wave_handover: The active lane finishes standing, then the next lane starts on cue. The 2-second change (3 seconds for floor teaching) is a cue change, not relocation. Athletes stay in their own bays.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.equipment: Flat markers, bottles outside active rectangles, clean dry nonslip surface. No partner support, unstable props or unverified anchor is assumed.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.setup_before_clock: Mark/inspect space before class. Readiness/restriction information must be available. First demonstration includes stop cue and immediate comfort check. Unknown restrictions or inability to follow safe directions require individual resolution, never assumed clearance.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.clock_definition: Row time = demonstration + waves × individual execution envelope + explicit wave handovers + reset/transition. The individual envelope includes stated steps, pauses and returns. Shared practice means separate bays, not 15 times one athlete dose.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.tempo_rule: Execution envelopes are estimates for the stated variant, not speed commands. If safe learning/movement needs longer, use contingency, remove optional work or revise the booking. Never rush to validate arithmetic.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.bay_to_target_transition: Base ends at 12:00 full or 7:00 compact with athletes standing in bays. Reserve exactly 180 seconds for exactly two parent-owned target tasks. The parent exemplar defines the split and charges bay-to-start gathering, demonstrations, observed holds, rehearsal, exit and return within those 180 seconds. Use the parent-defined allocation; do not double-charge gathering or hide it before the base ends.
layout_and_timing_assumptions.physical_validation_status: UNVERIFIED: measured space, body fit, sightlines, surface, shared-floor schedule and target corridors have not been observed. Arithmetic does not certify physical feasibility.

teaching_and_competency_policy.full_familiar: Sixteen ordered slots with reminder demonstrations only. SP-11/SP-12 explicitly repeat mastered A-March because exact B/C identities are unverified.
teaching_and_competency_policy.compact_familiar: Eleven slots in original relative order. Omit SP-04, SP-10, SP-11, SP-12, SP-14. Retain floor purpose through the declared stationary-bear modification; hinge and squat remain last.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_full: Eleven recognizable slots in 12 minutes. Easy march replaces jog; optional crossing/flight/B/C complexity is omitted; lunges lose rotation/depth; floor flow becomes knees-down rock-backs; descent is slow; basic march/foot-roll precede observed hinge and partial squat-to-stand. After the easy raise, all actions are demonstrated and observed in three five-athlete waves.
teaching_and_competency_policy.or01_compact: Same eleven recognizable slots in 7 minutes. Basic walking/stepping/foot-roll can follow the coach in separate bays. Lunge, floor, slow drop, hinge and partial squat remain serialized in three observed five-athlete waves. One hinge and one squat cycle are readiness observations; qualification belongs to subsequent instructional work.
deferred_complexity: Traveling bear crawl and new complete plank/downward-dog flow
Full toe/ankle contact and overhead squat-to-stand range when unavailable
teaching_and_competency_policy.what_deferred_means: Practice the simpler named component in its original place; log performed variant and unfilled demand. Teach additional complexity in a relevant later instructional module. Do not silently pass it, substitute a generic unrelated warm-up or add teaching outside the clock.
teaching_and_competency_policy.partial_competency: Existing evidence can support a familiar variation, independently of age. Preparation completion does not unlock a main family: no-flight lowering is not landing, marching is not running, rock-back is not tumbling, and no throw/cue gate is tested here.
teaching_and_competency_policy.correction_limit: Use visible contingency for actual slower movement or brief corrective repeat and record time/dose/contacts. If essential teaching remains incomplete, mark profile/session REVISE and use the 12-minute instructional base or a justified booking adjustment. Never consume the reserved target time or speed up movement.
teaching_and_competency_policy.optional_reduction_order: For familiar full, remove SP-12 then SP-11, then SP-04/SP-10/SP-14 as readiness/purpose permits. Record omissions and revised clock. Compact/OR already omit these; beyond contingency, further necessary omissions require explicit review rather than an unqualified complete-base claim.

flight_not_qualified_overlay.application: For otherwise familiar athletes whose flight is unqualified, independent of age. This can accompany an independently qualified throw-only main branch, but does not itself authorize throwing or a cue.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-01: Easy march in place for the same 60 seconds full or 50 seconds compact; no flight.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-08: Retain a separately qualified no-flight rapid descent. If unlearned, slow drop squat to stick: 3 × 8-second envelopes, each 2 s lower + 2 s hold + 1 s stand + 3 s reset; no travel. Record changed variant.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-10: Omit four A-Skip hop landings; freed time is recovery, not another drill.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-13: Eight alternating no-flight foot-roll actions, four each side: 8 × 2 s + 4 s standing reset = 20 seconds; no travel. Log changed variant.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.SP-14: Omit six bilateral pogo landing events; no substitute jump.
flight_not_qualified_overlay.accounting: Subtract omitted flight events and record actual time/contacts. Reduced-impact preparation grants no JUMP-T, REACT-T, throwing, early-release or go/no-go qualification.

records.name: Easy jog
records.purpose: Raise temperature and establish stop-on-cue and personal-space behavior.

card_mapping_status.limit: This in-place delivery preserves the jog purpose; exact bay-delivery mapping remains unverified.

records.setup: Center of the personal bay; no traveling loop. Bottle outside active rectangle. The demonstration includes a stop-cue rehearsal and immediate comfort check.
cues: Small relaxed steps; speak easily.
Freeze in your own space on cue.
stop_rules: Cease for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, loss of balance or inability to follow the stop cue; coach checks readiness.

competency_rule.observe: Relaxed rhythm, conversational breathing and independent stop without crossing the boundary.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

full.variant: Easy jog in place
full.tempo: Natural easy cadence.
full.effort: Easy and conversational; no maximal speed, height, stretch or fatigue target.

rest.within_set: Only the pauses, resets and walking returns explicitly included in execution_segments.
rest.after_set: Use the row transition and next demonstration. Waiting waves add no repetitions. Extra required rest uses visible contingency, then an explicit reduction/revision.

full.other_contact_accounting: 60 seconds of easy jogging includes low flight/foot contacts. Actual number is not fixed: log duration and any counted contacts, never a fabricated fixed total.
full.prerequisite: Comfortable action, clear personal bay and ability to stop on cue.
full.count_definition: Time determines the dose; no repetition or contact count is predetermined.

count_reconciliation.calculation: Time dose; reps_total remains null.
count_reconciliation.partial_cycle_rule: A fraction in conversion arithmetic is not an accepted partial repetition. Record completed whole cycles/actions/sequences actually performed.

contact_accounting.landing_event_unit: One landing event after flight; bilateral landing is one event involving two feet.
contact_accounting.foot_contact_unit: One foot contacting the surface; bilateral landing contributes two foot contacts.
contact_accounting.task_contact_scope: Where numeric, excludes ordinary walking returns; it does not mean all task contacts follow flight. Other ordinary step/support counts remain in the per-side/segment detail or actual log.
contact_accounting.unknown_count_rule: Null means not predetermined or not a total-contact prescription; never coerce it to zero. A zero flight count does not mean zero standing/support/step contacts.

records.name: Backpedal
records.purpose: Rehearse controlled backward travel and orientation.

card_mapping_status.limit: A related backpedal-to-sprint identity is not this slow preparation task.

records.setup: Face the same end of the room. Mark 1 m behind the start; two short backward steps reach it, then two forward walking steps return. No turn or crossing.
cues: Short steps under you; look forward.
Check the clear space behind you before moving.
common_errors: Long reaching steps and backward lean.
stop_rules: Stop for obstacle, balance loss or pain; use ordinary walking return only when clear.

competency_rule.observe: Controls both backward steps and forward return with balance and stop-cue response.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Lateral shuffle
records.purpose: Access lateral movement with organized feet and controlled orientation.

card_mapping_status.limit: This low-intent short shuffle is not reactive cutting.

records.setup: Start centered. Step-close without crossing for 1 m right and 1 m left back to start. Repeat only for the familiar dose.
cues: Stay facing forward; step then close.
Own the stop.
common_errors: Reaching past the bay or racing the return.
stop_rules: Stop if feet collide, boundary control fails or discomfort appears.

competency_rule.observe: Maintains forward orientation and controlled step-close both directions.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog (ordered slot)
records.purpose: Prepare shoulder/wrist support, trunk control, hip movement and floor transitions with low fatigue.

verified_local_names: Inchworm → plank → bear crawl → downward dog
Inchworm to World’s Greatest Stretch (related legacy flow)
card_mapping_status.limit: Exact composite not established. Stationary limb unloads explicitly replace traveling bear crawl for 15-bay delivery. Knees-down rock-backs are a declared partial-purpose regression, not an exact approved composite. The proposed stationary substitution is specifically four separately mastered single-limb lifts with full replants, not an unspecified weight shift or contralateral crawl.

records.setup: One athlete per dry nonslip 3 m × 3 m bay. Entire floor footprint fits before use. No shared slow-crawl lane or following crawler. Coach checks hand/knee comfort before support. Familiar bear support uses one limb at a time: left hand, right hand, left foot, right foot. A lift means the whole selected hand or foot briefly clears the floor by about 1–2 cm; it is not merely a weight shift. Fully replant and settle before the next limb.
cues: Hands comfortable; breathe with controlled trunk.
Quiet unhurried transitions; soft knees in downward dog.
Keep the trunk quiet; lift one contact only, then fully replant before the next.
Do not lift opposite hand and foot together.
common_errors: Forced straight knees or shoulder range.
Starting the next lift before the previous contact is fully replanted.
Rotating or sagging the trunk to clear the limb.
stop_rules: Stop for wrist/shoulder pain, slipping, trunk-control loss or inadequate footprint.
Use contingency or record incomplete rather than rushing floor entry.

Omit the familiar bear-lift component if any single-limb lift/replant has not already been mastered; use the entire named instructional floor profile and its coaching clock, or record incomplete purpose. No new bear-lift teaching is assumed inside the familiar reminder.

competency_rule.observe: Comfortable actual support and floor entry/exit. Rock-back does not pass plank/bear or tumbling support. For familiar bear lifts, each selected contact clears briefly, fully replants, and the trunk remains quiet before the next lift.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

records.name: Ankling
records.purpose: Rehearse comfortable small ankle/foot action and rhythm.

card_mapping_status.limit: Combined legacy name is not one verified current variant. In-place no-flight foot-roll is a declared learning regression.

records.setup: Tiny forward steps within 1 m; walk back after the pass. First visit stays in place with both feet available for balance.
cues: Small comfortable foot action beneath hips.
Let the foot move naturally.
common_errors: Large knee lifts or extra hopping.
stop_rules: Stop for foot/ankle discomfort, uncontrolled impact or lost rhythm; use no-flight option only when comfortable.

competency_rule.observe: Controls the actual low-demand foot action; not a sprint/reactive-ankle qualification.
competency_rule.pass_scope: Preparation observation only. A completed repetition does not grant a main-family, loaded-strength, flight, throwing, cue-response or tumbling qualification.
competency_rule.record: Log selected profile, actual variant/dose, comfort, response to cue, omissions and not-observed actions. No actual results are invented.

card_mapping_status.limit: Source 62 is review state. Familiar prescription follows candidate variant sequential-bilateral-reach-squat-to-stand: standing hinge/contact, comfortable squat, one controlled overhead reach per assigned side, stand/reset. records.setup: Same three five-athlete observation waves. Comfortable stance/reachable contact points; no forced toe touch or depth. Coaches see feet and trunk. Familiar source-linked sequence assigns LEFT reach and return, then RIGHT reach and return while the opposite hand maintains its comfortable toe/ankle contact; stand only after both reaches. Each reach stays in controlled comfortable range.
cues: Use comfortable range and a stable foot.
Reach without forced rib flare; stand smoothly.
Left reach and return, right reach and return, then stand; do not skip a side.
common_errors: Counting one reach as completion of the familiar sequential-bilateral cycle.
stop_rules: Stop for pain or uncontrolled balance/trunk; use declared partial sequence if comfortable. Longer teaching uses contingency or records incomplete.

workload_and_tumbling_interface.purpose: Finish warm and organized, not tired. Effort about 2/10 and conversational; this is not overload or conditioning.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.full_flight: Four unilateral A-Skip hop landings and six bilateral pogo landing events are explicitly prescribed in the familiar full profile. Timed easy jog and ankling also carry impact; their actual flight/contact detail is recorded instead of fabricated.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.compact_flight: A-Skip/pogo are omitted, but easy jog still has impact and ankling actual contacts remain in the record. Compressed is not automatically impact-free.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.or01_flight: No intentional flight in the first-visit profiles; no landing gate is thereby passed.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.upper_body: Familiar floor work includes a 4-second high plank, brief bear-position support/unloads and downward-dog access. Count wrist/shoulder/trunk demand alongside throwing, pressing, bracing and separate tumbling. Rock-back support is still support.
workload_and_tumbling_interface.tumbling: The separate 30-minute tumbling/Body Control allocation remains unprescribed here. Share actual comfort, support/impact exposure and observations with its coach. Its later load and staffing remain unverified.

counting_conventions.primary_repetitions: Always interpret reps_total with count_unit and count_definition. Mixed flow constituents, side counts, foot contacts and timed segments are not interchangeable.
counting_conventions.segment_repetitions: Each execution segment has its own count_unit. Its duration remains repetitions × seconds_each. Primary count contributions convert the segment counts to the record primary unit; complete cycles remain the accepted unit.
counting_conventions.SP-09_and_fallback_normalization: A-March primary counts are now individual steps: 8 familiar (4 each side) or 4 OR (2 each side). Bilateral cycle counts are explicit secondary metadata; actual movement/time unchanged.
counting_conventions.SP-13_correction: Familiar full/compact is 16 individual ankling task contacts, eight each foot; OR01 full/compact is four individual foot-roll/replace actions, two each foot. No execution duration or physical dose changed.
counting_conventions.contact_rule: Landing events and per-foot landing contacts are separate. Timed jogging/actual ankling flight count stays null when not predetermined, never zero by default.
